title: [CQ-C06] Acknowledged context deltas
description:
Objective: Serve deltas only for the exact acknowledged base and receiver process incarnation.

Deliverable: Acknowledged context deltas. This is task C06 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): C05.

implementationPlan.description:
TESTS FIRST (red). C06 is the get_context wiring of the LANDED C06a module, packages/moe-daemon/src/context/contextDelta.ts (task-7d0f7f08): diffPackets, applyDelta, DeltaBaseStore, deltaBaseKey and decideDelta. Adapt to its landed names.

Create tools/getContextDelta.test.ts.
- Copy getContextReceipt.test.ts's fixture: ToolTestHarness, a worker that owns the task's RUNNING attempt, and get_context called with sessionId S.
- Assert exact objects and reasons, never truthiness.

Cases:
- D1, DoD1. Read 1 passes contextEpoch 0 and gets the full packet, with servedContext.contextDelta {served:'full', reason:'base-unavailable'}. Then change the task so that one served key disappears; pick a real present-then-absent key in the packet. Read 2 passes basePacketId = read 1's packetId and epoch 0.
  - It returns `delta` (C06a ContextDelta) in place of the packet body, with servedContext.contextDelta {served:'delta'}.
  - The vanished key's pointer is in `removed`.
  - applyDelta(parse(read 1 packet), delta) deep-equals a full read taken right after.
  - servedContext.packetId is that full result's packetId, and the receipt records it.
- D2: a basePacketId of an older packet gives full, base-mismatch.
- D3: a read with an epoch but no basePacketId gives full, no-base.
- D4, restart: a new harness/StateManager over the same .moe, where the persisted receipt still names the base, gives full, base-unavailable.
- D5, compaction: epoch 1 against a base stored under 0 gives full, epoch-changed. No epoch gives full, epoch-missing.
- D6, VM replacement or re-claim: a new attempt generation gives attempt-mismatch. A different sessionId gives session-mismatch.
- D7, DoD3: move the attempt to reconciling and back through moe.reattach_attempt in the SAME process. A basePacketId that the receipt and the stored base both name still gives full, phase-changed.
- D8, legacy: a read with neither basePacketId nor contextEpoch is byte-identical to today's packet, with no contextDelta key.
- D9: an unrecorded read (no sessionId, or a non-owner) that presents a base gives full, with the reason = its receiptStatus. Nothing is stored.

implementationPlan.description:
Wire deltas into packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getContext.ts.

Error handling: caller-shape errors throw INVALID_INPUT, and everything else falls back to a full packet; a delta path never throws.

Input schema:
- `basePacketId`: string, pattern ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$.
- `contextEpoch`: integer, minimum 0. The receiving session's compaction counter; a seat must advance it on every compaction.
Validate both before any read.

In servedContextIdentity, only on the 'recorded' path, after recordContextReceipt for the full result packet (text and packetId exactly as today):
- current = {attemptId, generation, sessionId, lastPhaseAt: attempt.lastPhaseAt, runner: processStartedAt and host ? `${processStartedAt}@${host}` : null}.
- stored = the store's get(deltaBaseKey(...)). The store comes from a module-level WeakMap<StateManager, DeltaBaseStore>, so a new StateManager (a restart) starts empty and tests stay isolated.
- decision = decideDelta({basePacketId, contextEpoch}, current, stored).
- When contextEpoch was presented, set the new base {packetId, text, ...current, contextEpoch}. Without an epoch, store nothing, so a later delta is impossible (fail closed).
- On a delta: return {delta: diffPackets(basePacketId, stored.text, packetId, text), servedContext: {...identity, receiptStatus:'recorded', receiptId, packetId, contextDelta:{served:'delta'}}}.
- Otherwise: return the full packet, with contextDelta {served:'full', reason} ONLY when the request presented basePacketId or contextEpoch. Unrecorded reads that present them get reason = receiptStatus.

Do not change the receipt shape, F06's packetId rule, view:'status', or reads that present neither field. Add one sentence to the tool description. docs/MCP_SERVER.md is left to the epic final C11's docs sweep; note that in the completion summary.

Make D1-D9 green.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review of the C06 diff (getContext.ts plus the test).

Fixed:
- The contextEpoch schema description said any read without an epoch clears the stored base. A read presenting neither field leaves the base alone (the legacy path, D8). It now reads: "A read without it never gets a delta; one presenting basePacketId also clears the stored base." That is the only byte change to getContext.ts since QA's sha 68f358a4.
- D8 now also proves that a legacy read keeps the base. Mutant m7, where a legacy read clears the base, is killed by D8.

Checked, theoretical, no change:
- Delta without the base held:
  - restart: a new StateManager has an empty store (D4);
  - re-claim or VM replacement: a new attempt or generation (D6), or a different runner (D6);
  - another session (D6);
  - compaction: needs an epoch bump (D5); with no epoch, there is never a delta and the base is cleared;
  - reattach: a reconcile moves lastPhaseAt (D7). A same-millisecond reconcile plus reattach is theoretical only: reconcileRunningAttempts runs only at startup, index.ts:539, on a fresh store. A running→running reattach is a no-op write, and only happens at session boundaries, where a new MOE_SESSION_ID gives session-mismatch.
- Reconstruction is pointer-based and deep-equal to the full packet (D1). It is not byte-equal (key order); packetId names the daemon's serialization, and C11's docs should say so. JSON text has no undefined values.
- Concurrency: tool dispatch holds the global mutex and deltaAgainstBase is synchronous, so the last write wins; a lost response leads to base-mismatch and then a full packet.
- Memory: at most 256 LRU entries, one per task; nothing stores one until activation.
- Legacy reads: response bytes unchanged (D8, plus getContext 47 and getContextReceipt 48 green).
- deltaAgainstBase's only throwing call (diffPackets) is caught; DeltaBaseStore and decideDelta do not throw.
- Forbidden-token grep: 0 hits. No .moe edits and no Git writes by me.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1. One task holding the pure module plus the wiring. About 400 lines over 4 files, right at the cap on a shared wire contract. Split: the pure module became C06a (task-7d0f7f08, with the exact interface in its description), and C06 is the wiring.
2. Detecting compaction in the daemon. Impossible: compaction happens inside one CLI process, with the same MOE_SESSION_ID. So the contract requires an explicit contextEpoch that the seat advances on compaction, and the absence of an epoch never gives a delta (fail closed). Seat-side reporting (the moe-compaction-keeper session.compact hook plus proxy stamping) is activation and a client consumer, so it is out of scope.
3. Persisting bases. Rejected: in memory means a restart naturally gives a full snapshot (DoD2), and there is no new store.
4. Treating reattach as continuity. Rejected by DoD3. lastPhaseAt changes on every reconcile and reattach, so a base served before one never matches after it, without editing reattach_attempt.
5. C05 is kept in dependsOn per the directive, but NOT consumed: deltas are generic JSON diffs, so source-reference and evidence changes appear as changed fields.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Landed:
- getContext.ts servedContextIdentity records a receipt only on the 'recorded' path (sessionId, a running attempt, owner = caller = assignee). packetId = sha256 of JSON.stringify(packet without servedContext).
- The attemptStore receipt is attempt.contextReceipt (latest wins). It records attemptId, generation, workerId, sessionId, packetId and planRevision.
- ExecutionAttempt.lastPhaseAt changes on every phase transition. processStartedAt and host are the runner identity.
- The seat sessionId is MOE_SESSION_ID `<workerId>@<preflight-iso>`, one per CLI launch, and stays the same across compactions.

Assumed: the C06a names in task-7d0f7f08's description.
planningNotes.risks:
- The epoch is client-asserted. Until a seat stamps it mechanically, nothing sends contextEpoch, so no delta is ever served: safe by construction.
- Key order: diff and apply only by pointer, never by comparing text.
- Receipt semantics: the receipt names the reconstructed full packet, which is what the session now holds (base + delta).
- Size is at most 400 net lines.
- Shared contract: run the full suite.
